title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a Z_p-algebra and S_k = k{T} is the divided-power polynomial algebra in one variable. Put T_r = T^{[p^r]}.

(1) Key relation. One has (T^{[n]})^p = ((pn)!/(n!)^p) T^{[pn]}. For n = p^r write
T_r^p = p! · ν_r · T_{r+1}, with ν_r = (p^{r+1})!/(((p^r)!)^p p!).
Legendre's formula gives v_p(ν_r) = 0, so ν_r is a unit. Hence the boxed relation T_r^p = p ν'_r T_{r+1}, with ν'_r = (p-1)! ν_r ∈ Z_p^*.

(2) Structure of S_k. Writing n = Σ i_α p^α in base p, T^{[n]} is a unit times Π T_α^{i_α}. So S_k is generated as an algebra by the T_r, with relations T_r^p = p ν'_r T_{r+1}.

(3) The truncated ideal. Let τ_{p^r}S be the ideal of degrees ≥ p^r. It has basis the monomials with some i_α ≠ 0 for α ≥ r. As an S-module it is generated by t_s = T_s (s ≥ r), with relations T_s^{p-1} t_s = p ν'_s t_{s+1}. Implicitly there are also the obvious relations T_{s'} t_s = T_s t_{s'}, which the page does not write.

(4) The problem. Classify S-linear maps u : τ_{p^r}S_k → S_k ⊗_k M (the target is crossed out; probably M ⊗ S, or an Ω ⊗ S). These are homogeneous of degree -d with d < p^r, d = d_0 + d_1 p + … + d_{r-1} p^{r-1}. Such a u is given by elements y_s = u(t_s) ∈ S^{(p^s-d)} ⊗ M subject to (R_s): T_s^{p-1} y_s = p ν'_s y_{s+1}.

(5) Base-p digits of p^s - d. Let ν = v_p(d). Then
p^s - d = p^ν(δ_ν + δ_{ν+1} p + … + δ_{r-1} p^{r-1-ν} + (p-1)p^{r-ν} + … + (p-1)p^{s-ν-1}),
with δ_ν = p - d_ν and δ_i = p-1-d_i for i > ν. So S^{(p^s-d)} is free of rank one, generated by
mono_s = T_ν^{δ_ν} ⋯ T_{r-1}^{δ_{r-1}} (T_r ⋯ T_{s-1})^{p-1}.

(6) Implicit conclusion (the page stops just before it). Write y_s = mono_s ⊗ m_s. Since T_s^{p-1} mono_s = mono_{s+1}, relation (R_s) becomes m_s = p ν'_s m_{s+1}; the cross relations are then automatic.
- Degree -d maps u correspond to sequences (m_s)_{s≥r} in M with m_s = (unit)·p·m_{s+1}.
- That is, to lim(… → M →p M →p M), roughly Hom(Z[1/p], M) up to units.
- Hence such Hom groups detect p-divisibility of M, and vanish for M p-adically separated and without infinitely p-divisible elements.

Purpose: a local computation in one variable, plausibly toward duality or Hom/Ext computations for truncations (Hodge-type filtration) of PD-polynomial algebras in the 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex.
errors: No mathematical error found. The unit claims and the digit expansion of p^s - d check out (δ_ν = (p-1)-(d_ν-1) = p - d_ν).

The presentation of τ_{p^r}S as an S-module omits the obvious relations T_{s'} t_s = T_s t_{s'}. They turn out to be automatically compatible once (R_s) is imposed, so this is a gap in exposition only.
The case d = 0 (ν undefined) is not treated separately.

ideas.what: Structure of the divided power algebra k{T} over a Z_p-algebra via the generators T^{[p^r]}, with T_r^p = p·unit·T_{r+1}
ideas.modern_name: Standard presentation of the PD polynomial algebra in characteristic p / mixed characteristic
ideas.where_published: Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (LNM 407); Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on crystalline cohomology

ideas.what: Presentation of the degree-truncated ideal τ_{p^r}k{T} by generators T_s (s≥r) and relations T_s^{p-1}T_s = pν'_sT_{s+1}; Hom of degree -d into S⊗M computed via base-p digits of p^s-d
ideas.modern_name: Hom/duality computation for PD-filtration pieces; leads to an inverse limit along multiplication by p

missed.claim: The computation implicitly shows that S-linear maps τ_{p^r}k{T} → k{T}⊗M of degree -d correspond to p-divisible sequences m_s = p·unit·m_{s+1}, i.e. to lim_p M. This is non-trivial only for M with infinitely p-divisible elements. The page stops before stating it.
missed.quote: T_s^{p-1} y_s = p ν'_s y_{s+1} ... donc S^{(p^s-d)} a comme base T_ν^{δ_ν}…T_{r-1}^{δ_{r-1}}(T_r⋯T_{s-1})^{p-1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small instance of the pathology of PD-algebras (non-finite generation, R lim/p-adic completeness issues) underlying modern derived de Rham/crystalline comparisons. The result itself is elementary and essentially folklore.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine local computation with divided powers in one variable. It contains standard facts about k{T} and an elementary Hom computation, with no apparent new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The underbraced symbol in line 2 is ν_r (defined as p^{r+1}!/((p^r!)^p p!)), not γ_r.
Top right reads 'anneau de base k une Z_p-algèbre'.
The target of u is struck over; it is likely 'M ⊗_k S_k' or 'Ω ⊗ S_k' rather than a legible word.
The label to the left of the box u(t_s) = … is crossed out (not a clean '(R_s)'). Inside the box, y_s ∈ S_k^{(p^s-d)} ⊗_k M, preceded by a crossed-out expression.
The line 'donc les … de degré d < p^r' probably refers to maps u of degree -d with d < p^r.
